When she awakens, Shirou Emiya is gone.

Thinking he may be preparing their late lunch, she goes to the sitting room—but finds neither Shirou nor lunch.

“…He has gone out alone again. I told him to say something before leaving. Why will Shirou never listen to what he is told?”

Muttering to herself, she sits upon the veranda.

「……まったく。一人で出歩くのが好きなのは判りますが、これでは協力している意味がないではありませんか」
所在なげに足をぶらつかせる。
それもいつしか飽きて、物思いにふけるように視線をあげた。

pages.en:
“…Honestly. I understand that he enjoys wandering alone, but this rather defeats the purpose of our cooperation.”

With nothing to do, she swings her feet absently.

Eventually even that loses its appeal, and she raises her eyes as though sinking into thought.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Honestly. I know he likes to walk alone, but that takes away the whole meaning of our cooperation.”

天蓋めいた雲はゆっくりと流れており、遠くの空には切れ間が見えた。
この分なら、夜になれば晴れるだろう。
星が見えるようになったのなら、明日の事を占える。
昔、自分付きの魔術師に教わった星読みを、彼女はまだ覚えていた。

pages.en:
The sky is a single expanse of gray.

The canopy of clouds drifts slowly onward, with breaks already visible in the distance.

At this rate, the sky should clear by nightfall.

Once the stars emerge, she can divine what tomorrow will bring.

She still remembers the art of reading the stars taught to her long ago by the mage who attended her.

The canopy of clouds is drifting slowly and an opening can be seen in the distant sky.
It should be a clear sky tonight.
Once the stars can be seen, tomorrow can be predicted.

群がる危険を察しておいて、最も善き道を進ませるのだ。
彼女が心配する相手はともかく危なっかしいので、それぐらいはしないと安心して眠れないのである。

pages.en:
Until now, she has used it only for solemn questions, such as whether the path she followed was right. But tonight, she finds herself wanting to read the future of one particular person.

And if possible, to find a radiant tomorrow waiting for him.

She would discern every danger gathering around him and guide him down the best possible path.

The person she worries over is impossibly reckless. Unless she does at least that much, she will never sleep peacefully.

さて。問題はこの町から観測できる星の位置ですが」

彼女にとって優先すべきは聖杯戦争に勝ち残る事であり、誰かの為に星を読む事ではなかったからだ。
自分らしくないとは彼女だって分かっている。
それでも、それを知った上で星読みをしようとして、夜の帳を今か今かと待っている。
……まったく、凄まじいまでの心境の変化と言えよう。
これではまるで、物語に聞く恋する少女ではないかと苦笑し、遠くの空を眺め続ける。

pages.en:
“—Now. The difficulty is determining the position of the stars as seen from this city.”

Come to think of it, she has not once looked up at the night sky since arriving here.

Her first obligation was to survive the Holy Grail War, not to read the stars for someone else.

She understands that this is unlike her.

And despite understanding, she still means to perform the divination, waiting impatiently for night to lower its curtain.

…It is a remarkable change of heart indeed.

She smiles ruefully at the thought that she resembles a maiden in love from some old romance and continues gazing into the distant sky.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
Well. The problem is the stars that can be seen from this town…”
Come to think of it, she has never looked up at the sky until this day.
All she cared about was winning the Holy Grail War, and not reading stars for someone else.
She knows it’s not like her.
But she still tries to read the stars, and she waits for nightfall to come.
…Honestly, this is a big change in her thinking.
She continues to stare at the sky, thinking it’s just like the young girls in love she has read about in stories.

“Wh-what is it? I have certainly not surrendered to Shirou's banner or anything of the kind…!”
